note: DRAFT v1 module checks and final knowledge check for the CARSI Water Restoration Practitioner course. Original CARSI questions written for Australian conditions; no IICRC standard text reproduced. SME review and sign-off required before seeding.

quizzes.title: CARSI Water Restoration Practitioner — Module 1 check

questions.questionText: You arrive first at a water-damaged unit. What is your first task?
options: Make the site safe and size the loss
Start setting up air movers straight away
Pull up the carpet to check the underlay
Ring the insurer for an approval number
questions.explanation: The first hour is make safe and size the loss, not start drying. Sizing and safety drive every later decision, and machines come after the hazards are controlled.

questions.questionText: Which figure best sizes a water loss for the job file?
options: The number of towels used to mop
How worried the owner sounds
The age of the building in years
The affected floor area in square metres
questions.explanation: Affected area in m² is the measurable figure that sizes the loss and feeds the drying plan, the equipment and the quote. The others are not measurements.

questions.questionText: Why record the air temperature and relative humidity on arrival?
options: It is only needed for the invoice total
Insurers refuse claims without the weather
It sets the starting point for drying decisions
It decides the colour of the report cover
questions.explanation: The starting air condition (°C and %RH) is the baseline every later psychrometric decision and reading is compared against, so it is recorded at the first attendance.

questions.questionText: What is the correct order of the restoration arc?
options: Dry, make safe, verify, then understand the water
Make safe, understand, control source, assess, dry, monitor, verify, document
Document first, then dry, then make safe
Assess moisture, invoice, then control the source
questions.explanation: The arc runs make safe, understand the water and materials, control the source, assess moisture, dry, monitor, verify and document. Each step feeds the next, so order matters.

questions.questionText: A floor looks dry on the surface two days after a leak. What does that tell you?
options: Surface dryness is not proof the materials are dry
The job is finished and you can leave
The leak never actually happened
The underlay is guaranteed to be dry too
questions.explanation: A dry-looking surface can sit over wet skirting, wall base and underlay. Only measured readings against a dry standard prove a material is dry.

questions.questionText: A hose discharging about 2 L/min runs for 36 hours. Roughly how much water is that?
options: About 43 L
About 430 L
About 43 000 L
About 4320 L
questions.explanation: 36 hours is 2160 minutes, and 2 L/min × 2160 min ≈ 4320 L. Estimating the volume explains why even a slow leak over a weekend is urgent.

quizzes.title: CARSI Water Restoration Practitioner — Module 2 check

questions.questionText: A burst mains supply line floods a laundry. Which category is this, before any degradation?
options: Category 2 (grey water)
Category 3 (black water)
It is never categorised
Category 1 (clean water)
questions.explanation: A sanitary mains supply line is a clean source, so it starts as Category 1. Category describes likely contamination, and a clean supply carries none to begin with.

questions.questionText: Clean water sits in a warm, closed building for two days. What can happen to its category?
options: It always stays Category 1 forever
It automatically becomes Category 3 in an hour
It can degrade toward Category 2 or 3
The category is irrelevant after a day
questions.explanation: A category can worsen over time as clean water contacts soils and supports growth, so a Friday Category 1 loss may be reassessed worse on Monday.

questions.questionText: You are unsure whether water is Category 2 or Category 3. What is the safe call?
options: Assume the lower category to save money
Treat it as the worse category and reassess
Ignore the category and start drying
Ask the owner to decide for you
questions.explanation: When unsure, treat water as the worse category and reassess. That protects people, and the reasons for the call are recorded in the job file.

questions.questionText: What does the class of a water loss describe?
options: The amount of water and how hard it is to dry
How contaminated the water is
The price of the job in AUD
Which insurer is paying the claim
questions.explanation: Class describes the quantity of water and the likely rate of evaporation — how big the drying job is. Contamination is category, which is a separate judgement.

questions.questionText: Water has soaked a ceiling, the wall insulation and the carpet from above. Which class is most likely?
options: Class 1 (least water)
Class 2 (a whole room, wicking to about 300 mm)
No class applies to ceilings
Class 3 (greatest amount, often from above)
questions.explanation: Saturation of ceilings, walls, insulation and subfloor, often from above, is Class 3 — the greatest amount of water and the most drying capacity needed.

questions.questionText: Wicking reaches 300 mm up the walls over a 6 m perimeter. Roughly what wall area is wet?
options: About 0.18 m²
About 18 m²
About 1.8 m²
About 180 m²
questions.explanation: 6 m × 0.3 m = 1.8 m² of wall. Reading the wicking height in millimetres lets you estimate the wetted area and size the class.

quizzes.title: CARSI Water Restoration Practitioner — Module 3 check

questions.questionText: There is standing water near a live 230 V power board. What do you do first?
options: Reach in and unplug the leads quickly
Start extracting the water immediately
Isolate the circuit at the board and confirm it is dead
Throw a towel over the board
questions.explanation: Water and 230 V mains are a fatal mix. Isolate the circuit at the switchboard and confirm it is dead before any contact — never reach into energised standing water.

questions.questionText: Under the model WHS laws, who holds the primary duty to control risks on the job?
options: The tenant who lives there
The PCBU conducting the business or undertaking
The insurer paying the claim
The neighbour next door
questions.explanation: The person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU) must eliminate risks so far as is reasonably practicable, or minimise them. The duty cannot be contracted away.

questions.questionText: Which control is the strongest on the hierarchy of controls?
options: Eliminating the hazard
Wearing a P2 respirator
Putting up a warning sign
Writing a safe work method statement
questions.explanation: Elimination sits at the top of the hierarchy; PPE and administrative controls are the least effective because they rely on human behaviour and do not remove the hazard.

questions.questionText: Which PPE set suits Category 3 (black water / sewage) work?
options: Gloves and a dust mask only
Nothing special is needed for sewage
A high-visibility vest and sunglasses
Fluid-resistant coveralls, boots, gloves, eye protection, and respiratory protection fit-tested to the wearer and fit-checked each time it is put on
questions.explanation: Category 3 means full skin protection plus P2 or higher respiratory protection fit-tested to the wearer and fit-checked each time it is put on, and everything contacted is treated as contaminated.

questions.questionText: Why must a tight-fitting respirator be fit-tested to the wearer?
options: It makes the mask last longer
It is only a paperwork requirement
It only works if it seals to the face
Fit has no effect on protection
questions.explanation: A respirator only protects when it seals. Without a good seal contaminated air leaks in and the wearer does not get the expected protection, so a mask that has not passed a fit test is not relied on. A quick fit check every time it goes on confirms the seal, but it does not replace the fit test.

questions.questionText: What should the job file record about PPE?
options: Only the PPE that was available in the van
The PPE actually used on the job
Nothing — PPE is never recorded
Only the cost of the PPE in AUD
questions.explanation: Record the PPE actually used, not just what was available, because the file must show the control that was in place at the time of the work.

quizzes.title: CARSI Water Restoration Practitioner — Module 4 check

questions.questionText: Which instrument gives a quantitative moisture reading inside a specific material such as timber?
options: A thermal imaging camera
A pin (resistance) moisture meter
A thermo-hygrometer
A tape measure
questions.explanation: A pin (resistance) meter reads moisture in a specific material. A non-invasive meter maps where moisture is; a thermo-hygrometer reads the air.

questions.questionText: A thermal camera shows a cold patch on a wall. What is the right next step?
options: Confirm it with a moisture meter before acting
Record it straight away as confirmed moisture
Ignore it completely
Start removing the plasterboard at once
questions.explanation: A thermal camera shows temperature, not water. A cold patch is a question, always confirmed with a moisture meter before any conclusion or removal.

questions.questionText: What does specific humidity in g/kg tell you that relative humidity alone does not?
options: The colour of the water
The price of the dehumidifier
The age of the building
How much water the air is actually carrying
questions.explanation: Specific humidity (g/kg) is the honest measure of how much water the air carries. Relative humidity moves with temperature and can mislead on its own.

questions.questionText: What is a dry standard (dry reference) reading?
options: A reading taken on the hottest day of the year
The number printed on the meter's box
The same material read in an unaffected area of the building
A reading taken only after the job finishes
questions.explanation: The dry standard is the same material, same instrument and mode, read in an unaffected part of the building. It becomes the drying goal for that material.

questions.questionText: Why read the same labelled points on every monitoring visit?
options: It makes the report shorter
So the readings are comparable and show a trend
It means fewer readings overall
It keeps the owner out of the room
questions.explanation: Reading the same labelled points each visit makes the numbers directly comparable and shows the drying trend toward the dry standard — the evidence the job is working.

questions.questionText: When is a drying job complete?
options: When affected materials reach the dry standard and readings are stable
After exactly three days, regardless of readings
When the room smells better
When the owner says it feels dry
questions.explanation: Drying is finished when every affected point reaches the dry standard and holds on the next visit — measured and stable, not assumed from feel or a fixed number of days.

quizzes.title: CARSI Water Restoration Practitioner — Module 5 check

questions.questionText: What are the four levers that control the rate of structural drying?
options: Evaporation, dehumidification, temperature and air exchange/containment
Price, speed, colour and brand
Water, fire, earth and air
Carpet, timber, plaster and tile
questions.explanation: The four levers are evaporation (air movers), dehumidification, temperature and air exchange or containment. Managing them together is what dries a structure.

questions.questionText: You run air movers in a closed, humid room with no dehumidification. What happens?
options: The room dries twice as fast
Nothing changes at all
The air movers remove the moisture themselves
Humidity rises, drying stalls and secondary damage is risked
questions.explanation: Airflow without moisture removal just lifts water into air that cannot hold more, so humidity rises, drying stalls and condensation or mould can follow.

questions.questionText: Air leaving the dehumidifier reads a lower g/kg than the air going into it. What does that show?
options: A new leak has started
The dehumidifier should be switched off
The dehumidifier is removing water from the air
The readings are not worth taking
questions.explanation: A lower g/kg at the outlet than at the inlet is direct evidence the dehumidifier is removing water. Comparing the drying zone with outside air is context only: dry outdoor air can make a zone that is drying well read wetter than outside, so confirm progress with material readings trending to the dry standard.

questions.questionText: In Australia, what total power does one 10 A circuit deliver, and why does it matter?
options: Unlimited power, so plug in as many machines as you like
About 2300 W — so you must budget machine amps per circuit
About 230 W — only one small fan fits
It does not matter on drying jobs
questions.explanation: 230 V × 10 A ≈ 2300 W per circuit, and outlets often share one breaker, so you add up machine current draws and keep each circuit safely under its rating.

questions.questionText: An LGR dehumidifier draws 4.5 A and each air mover draws 1.2 A. What is one dehumidifier plus four air movers?
options: About 9.3 A
About 5.7 A
About 2.4 A
About 20 A
questions.explanation: 4.5 + (4 × 1.2) = 4.5 + 4.8 = 9.3 A, which is too close to a 10 A circuit limit once start-up surges are added, so the load is split across two circuits.

questions.questionText: Visible mould is present on a wet wall. What does the drying rule say about air movers?
options: Run the air movers harder to dry it faster
Air movers are always fine on any job
Switch everything off and leave the site
Do not run air movers; use dehumidifiers and air filtration under containment
questions.explanation: High airflow across mould aerosolises spores and spreads contamination. While mould is present, dry with air filtration and dehumidifiers under containment; air movers wait for a clearance.

quizzes.title: CARSI Water Restoration Practitioner — Module 6 check

questions.questionText: Which set of records belongs in a defensible water-damage job file?
options: A single one-line invoice
Only the final dry reading
The technician's memory of the job
Cause, category/class, dated photos, a moisture map, daily readings and recorded decisions
questions.explanation: The file records the loss, dated photos, a moisture map with the dry standard, the drying plan, daily metric readings, safety and who authorised each decision.

questions.questionText: When should the job file be built?
options: Months later, from memory
Only if a dispute arises
As the job happens, in real time
After the invoice is paid
questions.explanation: Build the file as the work happens. Records made at the time are accurate and are what an assessor or court will accept; reconstructed notes are weak.

questions.questionText: Which readings best prove that drying is working day to day?
options: The owner's opinion that it feels drier
Falling material readings toward the dry standard and a lower g/kg in the zone
The number of air movers running
How loud the equipment is
questions.explanation: Material readings trending to the dry standard, backed by a g/kg drop across the dehumidifier, are the measured evidence that drying is progressing. Outside g/kg is context, not proof.

questions.questionText: A scope change (extra drying days or removing a material) is needed. What do you do?
options: Get it authorised and recorded before acting
Just do it and sort the paperwork later
Never change the scope for any reason
Ask the neighbour for permission
questions.explanation: Changes to an agreed scope are authorised and recorded, not assumed. That keeps the claim defensible and protects the business and the customer.

questions.questionText: Under the Australian Consumer Law, which over-claim should a technician avoid?
options: Saying readings will be taken each visit
Explaining the drying plan in plain English
Quoting the price in Australian dollars
Promising a material is 'sterilised' or guaranteeing a fixed dry time
questions.explanation: Services must be provided with due care and skill and be fit for the stated purpose, so avoid over-claims like 'sterilised' or a guaranteed dry time you cannot control.

questions.questionText: How are quotes and invoices expressed for Australian restoration work?
options: In US dollars
In litres of water removed
In Australian dollars (AUD), noting GST where it applies
In whatever currency the owner prefers
questions.explanation: Pricing is in AUD with GST noted where it applies. Clear, dated, AUD pricing is part of the record an insurer and the consumer rely on.

quizzes.title: CARSI Water Restoration Practitioner — Final knowledge check

questions.questionText: What is the professional aim of water damage restoration?
options: To make the room look tidy quickly
To replace everything that got wet
To return the structure and restorable contents to a dry, safe condition with evidence
To finish before the owner gets home
questions.explanation: The aim is a dry, safe condition achieved quickly and safely with measured evidence, and knowing when to restore a material rather than remove it.

questions.questionText: Water categories describe what?
options: How much water there is
How contaminated the water is likely to be
The price of the job
The brand of dehumidifier used
questions.explanation: Category is about likely contamination (Category 1 clean, 2 grey, 3 black). The amount of water and drying difficulty is the separate idea of class.

questions.questionText: A toilet overflow contains urine but no faeces. What category is it, typically?
options: Category 2
Category 1
Category 3
No category
questions.explanation: Grey water containing urine but no faeces is typically Category 2, recorded with its reasons and watched for degradation toward Category 3 over time.

questions.questionText: Which is the strongest control under the hierarchy of controls?
options: Personal protective equipment
A warning sign
A safe work method statement
Eliminating the hazard
questions.explanation: Elimination removes the hazard and is the most effective control; PPE and administrative controls are the last and least reliable lines of defence.

questions.questionText: You must work near standing water and a live 230 V supply. What comes first?
options: Start extracting and watch for sparks
Wear thicker gloves and carry on
Isolate and confirm the power is dead, and use an RCD
Nothing special is required
questions.explanation: Isolate the circuit, confirm it is dead, and run portable equipment through an RCD on tested-and-tagged leads. Water and 230 V mains can be fatal.

questions.questionText: Which instrument reading is the honest measure of how much water the air carries?
options: Relative humidity alone
Specific humidity in g/kg
The air temperature alone
The dew point in percent
questions.explanation: Specific humidity (g/kg) states the actual moisture the air carries. Relative humidity changes with temperature, so it can mislead when used on its own.

questions.questionText: How is the drying goal for a material set?
options: From a dry-standard reading of the same material in an unaffected area
From a round number everyone uses
From the owner's guess
From the air temperature outside
questions.explanation: The dry goal is the dry-standard reading taken from the same material, same instrument and mode, in an unaffected part of the same building.

questions.questionText: Why does airflow without dehumidification stall drying in a closed room?
options: The air movers run out of power
The carpet absorbs the air
It does not stall; it always speeds drying
Moisture is lifted into air that cannot hold more, so humidity rises
questions.explanation: Evaporated water has nowhere to go without dehumidification or exchange, so humidity climbs, drying stops and secondary damage is risked.

questions.questionText: One 10 A circuit at 230 V delivers roughly how much total power?
options: About 230 W
About 23 000 W
About 2300 W
Unlimited
questions.explanation: 230 V × 10 A ≈ 2300 W. Because outlets often share one breaker, you budget machine current draws so a circuit is not overloaded overnight.

questions.questionText: Visible mould is on a wet wall you are drying. What does the rule require?
options: Run air movers to dry it faster
Hold the air movers; use dehumidifiers and air filtration under containment
Ignore it and keep drying as normal
Spray it and switch on all the fans
questions.explanation: Air movers aerosolise mould spores, so they are held until remediation and a clearance; meanwhile dehumidifiers and air filtration run under containment.

questions.questionText: What is the best protection if a claim is questioned months later?
options: A clear, dated, measured job file
A good memory of the job
A friendly phone call to the owner
A higher price next time
questions.explanation: A dated file with photos, a moisture map, daily readings trending to the dry standard and recorded decisions is the proof that defends the work.

questions.questionText: Which statement about pricing and claims in Australia is correct?
options: Price in US dollars and skip GST
Never provide a quote
Guarantee a fixed dry time to win the job
Price in AUD with GST where it applies, and get scope changes authorised
questions.explanation: Australian work is priced in AUD with GST noted; scope changes are authorised and recorded, and over-claims such as a guaranteed dry time are avoided.
